fact: Circular 9/2026 of the Central Bank of Libya lets licensed e-payment companies issue e-wallets, including to legally resident foreigners, with daily transfer caps of 100,000 dinars person to person, 500,000 person to company and 2 million company to company for citizens.
Libya had 186,817 electronic wallets with 6,096 acceptance points and 681,092 transactions worth 92.08 billion dinars in 2025 to 15 February 2026, per data published by the Hukumatuna platform.
Jumhouria Bank launched an e-payment service for petrol stations through the OnePay - Mini Pay platform in the Masrafi Plus app, without commission fees (Libya Herald).

The Central Bank of Libya reports its LYPay service had 1,278,783 individual and 8,814 merchant subscribers and 102,059 purchases and transfers worth 285.8 million LYD from 1 August to 26 December 2024.
Governor Issa said digital-wallet transactions rose from 109 million dinars in October 2024 to 703 million dinars in August 2026.

Central Bank of Libya circular 9 of 2026 regulates e-wallet service from licensed payment companies, with daily caps of LD 100,000 person to person and LD 500,000 person to company for citizens, and LD 50,000 and LD 100,000 for resident foreigners.

Libya had 187,335 electronic wallets with 6,096 acceptance points in January-February 2026, and instant payment services LYPay and OnePay handled transactions worth over 44.6 billion dinars, per the Central Bank of Libya.
The Central Bank of Libya reported e-payment transactions of LD 389 billion in 2025, up 186% from LD 136 billion in 2024.
